title: Day 31 in a 30-day month uses the month's last day
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure customer A holds the shop's own term A, due on day 31 of the following month.
  • Make sure work order 1 for customer A is complete and ready to invoice (every part received, review done).
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1's Finance tab.
  2. Set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  3. Set Invoice Date to Mar 15, 2027.
  4. Set Invoice Date to May 15, 2027.
  5. Set Invoice Date to Aug 15, 2027.
  6. Set Invoice Date to Nov 15, 2027.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The invoice preview shows Invoice Date and Due date.

Step 2:

  • The Due date reads Nov 30, 2026 (November has 30 days).

Step 3:

  • The Due date reads Apr 30, 2027 (April has 30 days).

Step 4:

  • The Due date reads Jun 30, 2027 (June has 30 days).

Step 5:

  • The Due date reads Sep 30, 2027 (September has 30 days).

Step 6:

  • The Due date reads Dec 31, 2027 (December has 31 days).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R3: “When the following month is shorter than the term's day, the due date is that month's last day: day 31 invoiced in October is due Nov 30; day 30 or 31 invoiced in January is due Feb 28 (Feb 29 in a leap year); day 31 invoiced in March is due Apr 30.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf), read 23 Oct 2026: page "9 Invoice due date" ("Invoice Oct 28: still due Nov 10"). Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the PRD quotes.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ct-p9-03-invoice-oct-28-still-due-nov-10.png

The design's own words:

  • “Always the next month, even when the 10th of this month is still ahead or nearly here. Day 31 in a 30-day month uses its last day (Nov 30).”
